The rule that order quantity must be positive is a domain invariant of the order (domain kind), but the presentation controller decides it here instead of OrderService (application) or OrderEntity (domain)
Everything else in the file fits the presentation layer: @Controller('orders'), @Post(), @Get(':id'), @Body(), @Param() from @nestjs/common, and calls to orderService.create/findOne
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is in the presentation layer. Most of it fits that role: NestJS @Controller/@Post/@Get/@Body/@Param decorators, a constructor that injects OrderService, and methods that hand work to the service. But OrderController.create checks the rule that an order's quantity must be positive (`dto.quantity <= 0`) and rejects the request itself. That rule is an invariant of the domain order, not a delivery concern. The domain entity or the application service should enforce it, for example inside OrderService.create or OrderEntity. As written, the rule lives in the controller and is skipped by any other caller of OrderService.create. The candidate flags (1 branch, 1 comparison, 1 validation throw) match the source. Confidence is moderate because a positivity check can also be read as input validation at the boundary. Even so, the rubric treats a domain invariant decided in a presentation file as a violation, and the usual NestJS way is a DTO validator or a domain-level check.
